gaps.sentence: If it ___ tomorrow, the match will be cancelled.
gaps.explanation: In first conditionals the if-clause takes the present simple even with future meaning: rains.

gaps.sentence: He would be healthier if he ___ so much red meat.
gaps.hint: an unreal present habit, past simple
gaps.explanation: For an unreal present habit, the if-clause uses the past simple: did not eat.

gaps.sentence: He wouldn't be so tired today ___ so late last night.
gaps.explanation: Past condition with present result: if + past perfect, would + infinitive.

gaps.sentence: If only I had taken that job — I ___ much happier now.
gaps.hint: mixed wish: past event, present result
gaps.explanation: 'Now' anchors the result in the present, so 'would be' is needed.

gaps.sentence: You can stay out late as long as you ___ me a text when you arrive.
gaps.hint: as long as plus present simple
gaps.explanation: 'As long as' introduces the condition and takes the present simple: send.

gaps.sentence: He always carries a power bank in case his phone ___.
gaps.hint: in case plus the present simple
gaps.explanation: 'In case' takes the present simple for things that might happen: dies.

gaps.sentence: What will you do if the train ___ before you get there?
gaps.explanation: Even in questions about the future, the if-clause uses the present simple: leaves.

gaps.sentence: If you ___ late again, the manager will have to speak to you.
gaps.hint: a warning about a real future
gaps.explanation: A real warning about the future keeps the if-clause in the present simple: are.
